reader.requirement: At --std 85 any number of level-66 RENAMES entries may follow one logical record (in the File, Working-Storage or Linkage Section), each an independent alias, overlapping or not, with or without THRU, and several records may each carry their own RENAMES entries; none may be refused for being one more entry.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel >= 2002: whether a RENAMES operand is looked up in the record's subtree (2002+) or scope-wide with explicit qualification required (1985); not a count limit

reader.edition-search: Read BindRenames (owner.Renames66.Add, no count check) and the ResolveRedefinesPass loop over every Renames66 entry; grepped both and VersionConformancePass/Editions for renames with Edition/DialectLevel/Year: no edition test limits how many entries a record takes; the one edition consultation on the path is the operand-lookup arm.

reader.notes: The binder appends every level-66 entry to its record's Renames66 list without a limit and the resolve pass binds each independently, so any number of entries, overlapping, across sections, works at 85. The rule is permissive, so its refusal half is empty; the ODO refusal shown belongs to SR3/SR6.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 over the logical-record kinds the reader did not reach: c3_link (Linkage Section record of a contained program, four entries, overlapping, THRU/THROUGH/no-THRU, a MOVE through R4 back to the caller): printed 'R1=ABCD R2=CDEF R3=EFGH R4=GH / W=ABCDEFXY'; c3_sd2 (SD records, two records each with its own entries, through SORT INPUT/OUTPUT PROCEDURE): printed 'SR1=AAYY SR2=YY SR3=AAYY / SR1=BBXX SR2=XX SR3=BBXX'; c3_fd2rec (one FD, two 01 records, each followed by its own two entries): printed 'QA=ABCD QB=CD QC=ABC QD=D'; c3_dupname (two records each carrying 66 R and 66 S, referenced R OF G1, R IN G2: data-name-1 qualified by its 01 per SR3): printed 'R1=ABCD R2=WXYZ S1=CD S2=WX'. Control: c3_sd's RENAMES of an 01 refused COBOL2740 (SR4), not for the count.
